chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is befitting for those sitting in the summer that there be between every two people a distance equal to the length of an arm bone, so that one does not find it burdensome upon the other due to the heat.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended distance between people sitting in summer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Islamic principle of *adab* (etiquette) by linking physical comfort to social harmony. It underscores the Prophetic tradition of preventing *adha* (harm or inconvenience) to others in communal spaces, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding public conduct.
